craft_claim: A play frame brackets consequence; applied to genuine, present stakes it can read as trivialization or emotion invalidation, so the tone must yield at stakes peaks.

supporting_evidence.location: Mimesis as Make-Believe (Harvard UP, 1990), ch. 1 on props and fictional truths
supporting_evidence.note: Make-believe engagement is a game with props; treating a real situation as an object of make-believe denies its actual consequences, which is precisely what misfires when stakes are live.

supporting_evidence.location: Steps to an Ecology of Mind (1972), pp. 177-193
supporting_evidence.note: The play-frame signal asserts that the action does not denote what the real action would denote; imposing that frame on real harm is a category error.

supporting_evidence.location: Cross-link (read-only shared claim); Wood et al. 2009; Zielinski et al. 2023
supporting_evidence.note: Positivity that invalidates negative emotion can backfire; framing real distress as play is the same invalidation move in a comic key.

counterevidence.note: Humor can coexist with negative emotion when a violation stays benign; the risk is not emotion itself but a frame that tells the reader their live stake is not real.

scope: Stakes peaks and direct address of suffering.
exceptions: Tragicomedy and dark comedy deliberately hold both registers; that is an integration pattern governed by the genre engine, not a licence to trivialize.
